children: Investors feared artificial intelligence would disrupt traditional software. Snowflake says it is instead encouraging customers to store, process and spend more.
Snowflake delivers a warm surprise
Snowflake shares
surged more than 23% in late trading after the cloud-data company comfortably beat expectations.
Adjusted earnings reached $0.62 per share versus $0.45 forecast, while quarterly revenue rose 35% to $1.55 billion, topping Wall Street’s $1.48 billion estimate.

Product revenue — the money generated from customers on Snowflake’s platform — jumped 37% to $1.49 billion. Growth accelerated for a third consecutive quarter, an important reversal for a company whose consumption-based model previously suffered when customers became unusually enthusiastic about optimizing their cloud bills.

Snowflake added 692 customers during the quarter, including 14 members of the Forbes Global 2000. It now has 828 customers generating more than $1 million in annual product revenue, up 27%. Apparently, the snowball becomes easier to roll once enterprise budgets join in.
AI becomes an accelerant

Management said AI products generated roughly half of Snowflake’s recent growth acceleration. Cortex Code, its AI coding assistant, has reached more than 9,100 accounts, while collaborative enterprise tool CoWork is used by approximately 5,800.
The business model helps explain the upside. Companies must organize, govern and process their data before deploying useful AI systems.
Those workloads generate additional computing and storage activity on Snowflake’s platform. AI therefore creates new revenue while increasing demand for the company’s existing services.
Snowflake also has a five-year,
with Amazon Web Services covering cloud infrastructure, AI development and customer migrations.

The arrangement gives Snowflake capacity and distribution while helping businesses move from experimental chatbots toward applications employees might occasionally use without an executive demonstration.
Guidance raises the temperature
Snowflake lifted its fiscal 2027 product-revenue forecast to $6.07 billion from $5.84 billion, implying growth of approximately 36%.
Third-quarter product revenue is expected between $1.588 billion and $1.593 billion — well above the roughly $1.5 billion analysts anticipated.

The company also raised its adjusted operating-margin outlook to 14.5% from 13.5%, suggesting revenue is growing faster than operating costs. However, AI workloads require more computing power, prompting Snowflake to lower its product gross-margin forecast to 74%.
One further caution: Snowflake remains unprofitable under standard accounting rules and recorded around $423 million in stock-based compensation.
The rally rests on continued growth and eventual operating leverage. Anyway, the breakout is powerful — but after a 20% gap, guidance must now support a considerably taller valuation.

title: SNOW: Snowflake Stock Soars 23% on AI-Fueled Beat and Raised Outlook
